AttentionItem.description:
An engagement on the "needs attention" list, with the reason it surfaced. Mirrors the
SPA's `AttentionItem`; ordered worst first.
AttentionItem.title: AttentionItem

HealthBucket.description:
One bucket of the project-health breakdown. Mirrors the SPA's `HealthBucket` —
`pct` is the share of the *active* portfolio, 0-100.
HealthBucket.title: HealthBucket

PersonIn.description:
Add a roster person. `ref` (`p01`) is the stable handle the rest of the product joins
on — the timesheet and standup services carry it as a plain string, so it is immutable
once created.
PersonIn.title: PersonIn

PersonOut.description:
Mirrors the SPA's `Person`. `id` is the person's stable `ref` (`p01`) — the value every
`owner_id` / `assignee_id` / timesheet `person_id` on the wire joins against. `uuid` is the
roster person's opaque id — the value the timesheet and standup write endpoints require as
`person_id`, since nothing else on the wire carries it.
PersonOut.title: PersonOut

PersonPatch.description:
Edit a roster person. Absent means "leave alone"; `ref` is immutable — it is the
cross-service join value.
PersonPatch.title: PersonPatch

ProjectIn.description: Create an engagement. `owner_ref` names an existing person by their `ref` (`p01`).
ProjectIn.title: ProjectIn

ProjectOut.description:
Mirrors the SPA's `Project`. `owner_id` is a person `ref`; `open_tasks` is the stored
open-work headline; money is minor units in `currency`.
ProjectOut.title: ProjectOut

ProjectSummaryOut.description:
The Overview's engagement-side rollup — the same arithmetic the SPA's `derive.ts` runs
over the project and task lists, exposed once so a reporting view can share it. The
time-side numbers (utilization, billable hours) live on the timesheet service's summary.

`tasks_due_this_week` counts open board cards due in the week containing `today`.
ProjectSummaryOut.title: ProjectSummaryOut

ProjectUpdate.description:
Edit an engagement. Absent means "leave alone". `code` is immutable — it is the URL key
and the timesheet `project_ref`, so a rename would silently orphan rows in another schema.
ProjectUpdate.title: ProjectUpdate

TaskIn.description: Create a board card on an engagement (named by its `code`).
TaskIn.title: TaskIn

TaskOut.description:
Mirrors the SPA's `Task` — one card on the board. `status` is the board stage;
`project_id` is the owning engagement's opaque id; `assignee_id` is a person `ref`.
TaskOut.title: TaskOut

TaskUpdate.description:
Move or edit a board card. Absent means "leave alone"; an explicit `null` on
`assignee_ref` or `due_date` clears it. `key` and `project_code` are immutable — a card
never changes engagement or human id through this route.
TaskUpdate.title: TaskUpdate

get.description:
How far behind the relay is. **Alert on `oldest_seconds`.**

A stalled relay is the platform's quietest failure. It selects, finds nothing,
logs nothing, sleeps, and loops — `attempts` never increments and `last_error`
stays null, so the process looks healthy indefinitely while the outbox grows
without bound and every consumer downstream starves.

Deliberately **not** part of readiness. A backlog is not a reason to take the
service out of rotation: refusing traffic would stop new events being written
without helping drain the ones already queued, which makes the incident worse.
This is a metric to alert on, not a health state.

Counted through the outbox engine, not the application one. The app role is
NOBYPASSRLS and this request binds no tenant, so through it `pending` would be
zero whatever the table holds — the probe that exists to expose the stall would
be wired to the same blind spot that causes it.
get.summary: Outbox depth and age — scrape this

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
